Job title: Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant

Location: Belfast

Start Date: September 2027

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech. .

Build your career on projects that help regenerate land, protect communities and support a more sustainable future. At Tetra Tech, you’ll work with experienced specialists on challenging geo-environmental projects while developing the technical skills, practical experience and professional confidence to succeed.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant, you will join our Geo team, delivering geo-environmental consultancy services supported by in-house ground investigation expertise. You will work across contaminated land, site investigation, groundwater, environmental due diligence and advisory services for clients in sectors including property and regeneration, defence estates and transport.

Your Impact in this position

You will support the design, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental ground investigations. Your responsibilities will include desktop studies, accurate collection and analysis of site data, ground gas and groundwater monitoring, assessment of findings and preparation of detailed technical reports. This is an excellent opportunity to gain varied project experience and progress your career across a diverse portfolio of work.

5 Core Capabilities

Ground investigation: Assist with planning, procuring, supervising and managing geotechnical and geo-environmental investigations across a range of sites and sectors.
Geo-environmental assessment: Develop your knowledge of contaminated land, site investigation, groundwater, brownfield redevelopment, environmental due diligence and geotechnical engineering.
Site data and monitoring: Collect and analyse site information accurately, including ground gas and groundwater monitoring data, to support robust technical assessments.
Technical reporting and GIS: Produce clear, detailed reports and use Geographic Information Systems to create, manage and analyse environmental and site information.
Professional development and teamwork: Work collaboratively, communicate effectively, use initiative and commit to studying towards a professional qualification as your technical capability develops.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

You will have, or expect to achieve, a minimum 2:1 degree in geology, engineering geology, environmental science or a related subject. Enthusiasm for geo-environmental consultancy, strong analytical, written, communication and presentation skills, and a commitment to learning are essential. Relevant experience, such as a work placement, is desirable. You will also need a full driving licence and ideally access to a vehicle.

Working Environment

Based in Belfast, you will work across office, project and site environments, with travel to client and investigation sites required. Hybrid working is available; however, as a graduate, you will spend more time in the office initially to support training, mentoring and your development. Greater flexibility may be available as your knowledge and confidence grow, subject to project and team requirements .

Application Closing Date: 31st October 2026

Assessment Centre to be held: February 2027

Job Description

As the Environmental Impacts Project Manager, you will lead the planning, delivery and commissioning of sustainability and environmental initiatives across the Leonardo Helicopters (LH) UK portfolio. Working collaboratively with key stakeholders and delivery partners, you will help ensure initiatives are delivered safely, efficiently and to the highest standards, while meeting agreed budgets, timelines and performance targets.

Your impact

This is not a traditional end-to-end project management role. While you will take ownership of projects and initiatives, the role is equally about identifying opportunities, bringing people together, influencing positive change and turning sustainability ambitions into meaningful environmental improvements. You will be a passionate advocate for sustainability, using your knowledge, initiative and influence to make a tangible difference across the organisation.

You will provide day-to-day leadership and coordination across environmental and sustainability initiatives, driving performance against key metrics, managing risks and dependencies, and supporting successful implementation.

A key part of the role will be ensuring that Site Facilities environmental and sustainability activities remain fully compliant with UK legislation, LDO UK and LH UK policies, standards and procedures. You will identify opportunities for continuous improvement, challenge existing ways of working and work with stakeholders to develop practical solutions that reduce environmental impact and support the organisation’s wider sustainability ambitions.

Success in this role will require more than technical and project management capability. You will demonstrate a proactive, collaborative and purpose-driven approach, taking ownership, building strong relationships and role-modelling the behaviours needed to influence change. You will be comfortable working across organisational boundaries, engaging stakeholders at all levels and using your passion for sustainability to inspire action.

For the awareness of internal applicants, this role is a JFF level 6. This position is predominantly site based in Yeovil, with occasional working from home.

What you will do as a Site Facilities Environmental Impacts Project Manager:

Provide professional/technical advice in support of the successful delivery of infrastructure projects contributing to the 5-year business planning cycle and delivery of long-term strategies.
Ensure that suitable and sufficient HSE arrangements are deployed and practiced on all projects in accordance with current UK Legislation, LDO UK Policies and Procedures and the LHUK HSEMSM.
Collaborate with specialists such as Energy Managers, Sustainability Managers and local Government Officials for Permits and Licences.
Ensure all legal requirements, building regulations, safety codes, safety inspections, and local and national regulations are met.
Manage HSE issues, ensuring Contractors have a safe working environment within which to operate.
Ensure compliance with the LHUK Facilities project governance processes.
Effectively manage the Site Facilities related elements of audits by Regulatory and Assurance Bodies and Internal Auditors, including ISO14001, ISO45001 and ISO50001.
Manage the delivery of the ISO 50001 Energy Management System for LHUK.
Manage external audits.
Conduct annual review with Integrated Facilities Management (IFM) Energy Partner.
Review and chair the monthly Utilities Working Group (UWG).

Responsible for the publication of monthly utilities management reports.
Act as lead for Yeovil Site Utilities management, including gas, water and electricity.
Manage the reduction of Utilities consumption as part of the LHUK commitment to the LDO UK Carbon Net Zero targets.
Ensure that LHUK is compliant with UK legislation for Utilities, including but not limited to CCA, CRC, CCL and Gas Safety.
Help drive innovative ways of working and tools for the wider Energy Decarbonisation Team.
Act as the lead for Social Value (SV) outputs from contract award.
Responsible for the management of EV provision.
Management of solar initiates, both internal and external to the Yeovil site.

Emergency Preparedness and Business Continuity

You may be called upon to support the LHUK Emergency Preparedness processes and procedures supporting the Command Emergency Control Centre (ECC), responsible for the management and delivery of the Site Facilities responsibilities, focussed on the management of incident consequences relating to People, Environment, Assets and Reputation (PEAR).

Willingness to attain Practitioner Membership Standard of the Institute of Sustainability & Environmental Professionals by the end of Year 2 in role, and attain Full membership by the end of year 5

Clear understanding of business and functional strategy and how the role contributes to business objectives.
Understanding of real estate, infrastructure and Facilities Management processes, including CDM.
Experience and knowledge of LHUK manufacturing processes.
Financial competence, including budgetary control.
Self-motivated, purpose-driven and proactive, with the ability to deliver positive environmental and business change.

jobs.title: Activating Agricultural Land Use for the Bernalillo County Community
jobs.description:
Bernalillo County, NM aims to improve residents’ quality of life and support small agricultural entrepreneurs through access to open space. The Executive Fellow will promote this goal by engaging internal and external stakeholders, researching agricultural hub models, and developing contract templates for small growers. As a result of this work, the Executive Fellow will help transform a 34-acre plot into land that promotes wellbeing, enables education, and unlocks opportunities for new farmers.

Fellowship Dates: October 26, 2026 – October 22, 2027

Salary:
Executive Fellows are FUSE employees and receive an annual salary of $95,000. Fellows can also access various health, dental, and vision insurance benefits. This amount is not representative of market-rate salaries for the experienced professionals in our program but is intended as compensation for a year of public service.

ABOUT THE FUSE EXECUTIVE FELLOWSHIP

FUSE is a national nonprofit dedicated to increasing the capacity of local governments to work more effectively for communities. We embed private sector executives in city and county agencies to lead projects that improve public services and accelerate systems change. Since 2012, FUSE has led over 400 projects in 58 governments across 26 states, impacting a total population equivalent to 1 in 10 Americans.

Executive Fellows are embedded in government agencies working with senior leaders for at least one year of full-time work. Prospective responsibilities may include thorough data analytics and research, developing enhanced operations and financial models, building change management and strategic planning processes, and/or building broad coalitions to support project implementation efforts. Executive Fellows are data-driven and results-oriented and able to effectively manage complex projects. They build strong relationships with a broad array of stakeholders, foster alignment within and across various layers of government, and build partnerships between governments and communities.

Throughout the fellowships, Executive Fellows receive training, coaching, and professional support to help achieve their project goals.

PROJECT BACKGROUND

Bernalillo County’s Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space aims to improve residents’ quality of life, with an emphasis on community health, economic development, and cultural heritage. Access to open space advances all three pillars. Parks and green space help people maintain their physical and mental health. Leasable plots would give agricultural entrepreneurs the chance to start or further their businesses with ensured access to land and lower capital requirements. Demonstration and education gardens allow the next generation to learn about their agricultural heritage. Additionally, as New Mexico’s farming community ages, encouraging young farmers to join the profession could help Bernalillo County preserve its food security.

To promote these goals, the County purchased a 34-acre property to steward as an agricultural open space. The land is across the street from a high school and less than a 10-minute walk from two other schools, making it ideal for educational use. After a round of planning and community engagement, the County decided to dedicate it to three main purposes: agricultural education, demonstration plots and gardens, and gathering space for educational and community events; leasable fields (approximately 0.25-2 acres each) for small growers (including graduates of the Department’s beginning farmer training program; and a habitat space with walking paths for conservation and recreation. These agricultural uses will support regenerative practices, including promoting food grown on public land. The Rio Grande High School cluster received a US Department of Education grant to carry out K-12 STEM pathways.

As the County finishes the planning phase for this property, it requires additional support to advance implementation of the master plan. The FUSE Executive Fellow will support the Bernalillo County Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space by facilitating and documenting stakeholder engagement, coordinating communications and updates about the site’s master plan, researching operational models, and creating contract templates for future growers. As a result of this work, Bernalillo County residents will be able to learn, play, gather, and grow businesses on this land.

PROJECT APPROACH

The first 90 days of the fellowship will focus on in-depth discovery and relationship-building. Beginning Fall 2026, the FUSE Executive Fellow will develop deep relationships with a broad range of stakeholders, including government (e.g., , school leadership, Ciudad Soil and Water Conservation District, County Extension, and ), local agri-food businesses (e.g., produce aggregators, South Valley Economic Development Center), community organizations (e.g., acequia associations, neighborhood associations) and community members (with an emphasis on Grow the Growers, Youth Ag Corps participants and residents living in the property’s walkshed). In addition, the Executive Fellow will review policies and best practices for creating inclusive open space and promoting small agriculture in communities similar to Bernalillo County.

Based on insights gathered, the Executive Fellow will develop and present proposed refinements to project goals, priorities, and anticipated deliverables for review and approval by the Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space and the Executive Sponsor.

Next, the Executive Fellow will engage internal and external stakeholders to advance implementation of the master plan. In addition, the Executive Fellow will conduct extensive research on how other communities have leveraged open space to promote small agricultural entrepreneurship. By the end of the fellowship, the Executive Fellow will have helped launch initial operations in part of the property and built the foundation the County needs to finish development and continue operations in the future. new_jobs.title: Activating Agricultural Land Use for the Bernalillo County Community
new_jobs.description:
Bernalillo County, NM aims to improve residents’ quality of life and support small agricultural entrepreneurs through access to open space. The Executive Fellow will promote this goal by engaging internal and external stakeholders, researching agricultural hub models, and developing contract templates for small growers. As a result of this work, the Executive Fellow will help transform a 34-acre plot into land that promotes wellbeing, enables education, and unlocks opportunities for new farmers.

Fellowship Dates: October 26, 2026 – October 22, 2027

Salary:
Executive Fellows are FUSE employees and receive an annual salary of $95,000. Fellows can also access various health, dental, and vision insurance benefits. This amount is not representative of market-rate salaries for the experienced professionals in our program but is intended as compensation for a year of public service.

ABOUT THE FUSE EXECUTIVE FELLOWSHIP

FUSE is a national nonprofit dedicated to increasing the capacity of local governments to work more effectively for communities. We embed private sector executives in city and county agencies to lead projects that improve public services and accelerate systems change. Since 2012, FUSE has led over 400 projects in 58 governments across 26 states, impacting a total population equivalent to 1 in 10 Americans.

Executive Fellows are embedded in government agencies working with senior leaders for at least one year of full-time work. Prospective responsibilities may include thorough data analytics and research, developing enhanced operations and financial models, building change management and strategic planning processes, and/or building broad coalitions to support project implementation efforts. Executive Fellows are data-driven and results-oriented and able to effectively manage complex projects. They build strong relationships with a broad array of stakeholders, foster alignment within and across various layers of government, and build partnerships between governments and communities.

Throughout the fellowships, Executive Fellows receive training, coaching, and professional support to help achieve their project goals.

PROJECT BACKGROUND

Bernalillo County’s Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space aims to improve residents’ quality of life, with an emphasis on community health, economic development, and cultural heritage. Access to open space advances all three pillars. Parks and green space help people maintain their physical and mental health. Leasable plots would give agricultural entrepreneurs the chance to start or further their businesses with ensured access to land and lower capital requirements. Demonstration and education gardens allow the next generation to learn about their agricultural heritage. Additionally, as New Mexico’s farming community ages, encouraging young farmers to join the profession could help Bernalillo County preserve its food security.

To promote these goals, the County purchased a 34-acre property to steward as an agricultural open space. The land is across the street from a high school and less than a 10-minute walk from two other schools, making it ideal for educational use. After a round of planning and community engagement, the County decided to dedicate it to three main purposes: agricultural education, demonstration plots and gardens, and gathering space for educational and community events; leasable fields (approximately 0.25-2 acres each) for small growers (including graduates of the Department’s beginning farmer training program; and a habitat space with walking paths for conservation and recreation. These agricultural uses will support regenerative practices, including promoting food grown on public land. The Rio Grande High School cluster received a US Department of Education grant to carry out K-12 STEM pathways.

As the County finishes the planning phase for this property, it requires additional support to advance implementation of the master plan. The FUSE Executive Fellow will support the Bernalillo County Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space by facilitating and documenting stakeholder engagement, coordinating communications and updates about the site’s master plan, researching operational models, and creating contract templates for future growers. As a result of this work, Bernalillo County residents will be able to learn, play, gather, and grow businesses on this land.

PROJECT APPROACH

The first 90 days of the fellowship will focus on in-depth discovery and relationship-building. Beginning Fall 2026, the FUSE Executive Fellow will develop deep relationships with a broad range of stakeholders, including government (e.g., , school leadership, Ciudad Soil and Water Conservation District, County Extension, and ), local agri-food businesses (e.g., produce aggregators, South Valley Economic Development Center), community organizations (e.g., acequia associations, neighborhood associations) and community members (with an emphasis on Grow the Growers, Youth Ag Corps participants and residents living in the property’s walkshed). In addition, the Executive Fellow will review policies and best practices for creating inclusive open space and promoting small agriculture in communities similar to Bernalillo County.

Based on insights gathered, the Executive Fellow will develop and present proposed refinements to project goals, priorities, and anticipated deliverables for review and approval by the Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space and the Executive Sponsor.

Next, the Executive Fellow will engage internal and external stakeholders to advance implementation of the master plan. This will include facilitating and documenting discussions with community members and potential partners, working with consultants and the Open Space Manager to promote the updated plan to the public, and engaging County officials to provide inputs and approve decisions as appropriate. The Executive Fellow will ensure consistent communication, effective community building, and appropriate follow-up on decisions affecting the property. When the Executive Fellow identifies a potential partnership, they will assist the stakeholder in formalizing and launching the collaboration. If successful, the Executive Fellow will have helped the County form the relationships and identify the input necessary for the project to be effective.

In addition, the Executive Fellow will conduct extensive research on how other communities have leveraged open space to promote small agricultural entrepreneurship. This will include how communities fund and manage ongoing site operations and how they structure leases and relationships with small growers to be fair and inclusive–with an emphasis on supporting new businesses with limited cash on hand. They will use this research to create an operational plan to guide future management and to develop contract templates for future lessees that include alternate payment options (e.g., labor in lieu of cash). If successful, the County will have the insights and tools they need to continue managing the land after development is complete.

By the end of the fellowship, the Executive Fellow will have helped launch initial operations in part of the property and built the foundation the County needs to finish development and continue operations in the future. The Executive Fellow will be responsible for working with the Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space staff to ensure knowledge transfer, facilitate introductions to new stakeholders, and handover of any remaining responsibilities prior to departure.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES

By October 2027, the Executive Fellow will have overseen the following:
External Community Building – Engage external stakeholders (including schools, community organizations, neighbors, and other partner agencies) to implement the master plan and foster partnerships for its development and use.
Internal Facilitation – Ensure master plan consultants receive and incorporate stakeholder input. Prepare materials for presentation to management staff and county officials.
Operational Plan – Conduct research on how other communities have successfully promoted small agricultural hubs. Identify potential models for ongoing operation and management. Develop an operational plan to guide the County’s work.
Contract Templates – Develop templates for land lease contracts. Include options for alternative forms of payment that are achievable for target lessees/users.

KEY STAKEHOLDERS

Andre Dickson, Director, Department of Parks, Recreation, & Open Space

Mari Simbaña, Open Space Manager, Department of Parks, Recreation, & Open Space
